newsitem.title: USA: Sinclair Broadcast to buy TV, radio from Heritage.
newsitem.headline: Sinclair Broadcast to buy TV, radio from Heritage.

text.p: Sinclair Broadcast Group Inc. Wednesday said it agreed to buy 24 radio and six television stations from Heritage Media Group for $630 million in cash.
The acquisition will occur when Heritage merges with News Corp. Ltd., which is expected to occur in the first quarter of 1998.
Included in the sale are television stations KOKH-TV in Oklahoma City and WCHS-TV in Charleston and Huntington, W.Va.
The radio stations include WRTH-AM in St. Louis and KKSN-AM in Portland, Ore.
The transaction is expected to be financed entirely with bank borrowings.

Under the terms of the agreement, Sinclair is required to divest KOKH-TV in Oklahoma City prior to closing. The transaction is subject to Federal Communications Commission and Justice Department approval.
On Monday, Baltimore-based Sinclair said two television stations it owns and three it operates will switch network affiliation to the WB Television Network from the UPN Network.
Under the deal, which covers 10 years, WB has guaranteed compensation to Sinclair of $64 million for the first eight years, and an additional $20 million over the final two years.

The deal covers Sinclair-owned KRRT-TV in San Antonio and and KOCB-TV in Oklahoma City. Also covered are WPTT-TV in Pittsburgh; WNUV-TV in Baltimore; and WSTR-TV in Cincinnati, all of which Sinclar operates.
Sinclair owns or provides programming services to 29 television stations in 21 markets.
